name: Diar il-Bniet
description: Restaurant named after a medieval fief; serves fresh local produce 'from their fields to your fork'; old Maltese eatery decor; runs culinary workshops; booking recommended.

name: Il-Barri
description: Off the main square; one of the first restaurants in the locality, 75 years, family-run; large good portions; rabbit stew a mainstay; underground WWII shelter beneath.
flags_notes: Street: Triq il-Kbira; locality Mgarr (Maltese: Mgharr)

name: Ta' Rikardu
description: In the Citadel; retains original decor; local favourites incl vegetable soup and rabbit stew; known for appetisers, local cheese and wine from the owner's vineyard and farm.

name: Il-Bitha ta' Doni
description: On a busy Rabat street near a small church; good ambience and relaxed atmosphere; authentic Maltese and Mediterranean food.

name: Ta' Marija Restaurant
description: Authentic Maltese fare, gastro-style cuisine, folklore show and music; family-owned; popular with locals and visitors.

name: Maxokk Bakery
description: Family-run bakery known for traditional ftira (Maltese pizza equivalent), oven-baked in an old brick oven; try with local cheeselets.
flags_notes: Entry number clipped at page edge; inferred 262. Street: St James St

name: Mekren Bakery
description: Freshly baked bread, ricotta pies and pizzas baked in an old oven still in use; family-run, in an old building.
flags_notes: Entry number partly clipped ('63'); inferred 263. Street: Triq Hanaq

name: Nenu the Artisan Baker
maps_search_string: Nenu the Artisan Baker, Valletta, Malta
description: Old bakery that supplied downtown Valletta, now a classic Maltese restaurant; the bakery can still be visited; traditional food with retained Maltese names; booking recommended.

name: Ta' Saminu Bakery
description: Small traditional bakery selling freshly baked bread, savouries and pastries; usually busy; no seating.

name: Sottovento
description: One of the best fish restaurants in the area; comfortable indoor and outdoor seating; very fresh fish; menu includes traditional fare; popular with locals and visitors.

name: Trabuxu Bistro
description: Appears only as a full-page photo caption; no numbered text entry on this page.
flags_notes: Caption-only mention; reconcile with a numbered entry if one appears in another file/page.

name: Birgu Wharf
description: Modernised wharf of Vittoriosa (former HQ of the Knights' and British Navy fleets); several places for lunch or dinner overlooking Dockyard Creek; restaurants serve local snacks, pizzas, fish and meat.
flags_notes: AREA/cluster of restaurants, not a single venue; triage should decide. Street: Xatt il-Forn

name: Coast @ Cassarini
description: Where land meets shoreline; terrace with scenery and sunset; traditional food with international influence; small hamlet around a creek; near the Blue Grotto.
flags_notes: Locality Wied iz-Zurrieq, Qrendi. Website 'coast-com.mt' may be a typo for coast.com.mt; verify. Street: Triq Is-Sajjieda

name: Tartarun
description: In Malta's largest fishing village; one of the best fish restaurants on the island; varied menu of traditional and culinary delights, nice wine list; booking recommended.

name: Hammett's Macina
street_address: Triq il-31 Ta' Marzu, Xatt Juan B Azopardo
description: Historic building on a busy creek in the Three Cities; menu mixes local culinary traditions with the European and Mediterranean influences of past occupiers; 'a taste of history'.
flags_notes: Street: Triq il-31 Ta' Marzu, Xatt Juan B Azopardo

name: Senglea Wharf
description: Faces Vittoriosa; wharf lined with eateries, most with indoor or outdoor seating; busy in summer; bustling seafront with entertainment.
flags_notes: AREA/cluster, not a single venue. Street: Xatt Juan B Azopardo

name: Valletta Waterfront
description: 18th-century warehouses modernised for the cruise-liner terminal and converted into restaurants; faces the Grand Harbour; wide variety of food; popular for lunch or dinner; very popular with locals.
flags_notes: AREA/cluster, not a single venue. Street: Triq il-Vittmi tal-Gwerra Furjanizi

name: Culto Caffetteria-Panineria
description: Small Italian-style cafe in baroque Valletta; a good place to stop for a sandwich between visits to the city's sites.
flags_notes: Page was photographed rotated. Street: 49 St John's St

name: Giorgio's Cafeteria
description: In central Sliema's shopping area; good lunches, snacks and sweets; large portions; popular with locals; can be hard to get a seat; open till late and good for a late dinner.

name: Carob Tree
description: A food court in the centre of St Julian's; 11 kitchens and bars offering a wide range of food and drinks; near the St Julian's coastline; good afternoon or evening stop.
flags_notes: Food court / multi-vendor destination. Photo on page 15. Street: Triq Mikiel'Ang Borg

name: Is-Suq tal-Belt
description: Food court in the restored 19th-century Valletta market; several restaurants from snacks to meat and fresh fish; seating all around including outside; supermarket on the lower level.
flags_notes: Food court / market hall. Photo on page 15. Street: Merchants St

name: Chocolate District
description: One of the latest outlets specialising in chocolate and its by-products; international and local varieties; a small, intimate cafeteria for a coffee while sampling.
flags_notes: Website printed as 'choclatedistrict.com' (sic) - likely typo for chocolatedistrict.com; verify. Street: Melita St

name: Ambrosia
description: In the centre of Valletta next to the Grand Master's Palace; a dining experience with a twist; different ambience; delicious food and sizeable portions.

name: Cafe Jubilee
description: Original concept started in Gozo, now several outlets (some abroad); nostalgic interior with theatre posters and hanging items; good, different, tasty food; indoor and outdoor seating on Victoria's main square.
flags_notes: CHAIN/multiple outlets; this entry is the Victoria, Gozo outlet. Street: Independence Square

name: Del Borgo
description: In the quiet narrow streets of Vittoriosa; a wine bar and eatery in an old building; seating both for dining and for socialising over wine, cheese and nibbles; very popular with locals.

name: Fontanella Tea Garden
description: Coffee, a beer or a drink on the bastions of medieval Mdina with magnificent views; popular cakes; a wine bar next door, good in the evening when Mdina is quieter; a favourite.

name: Victory Cafe
description: Inside one of Malta's best war museums (rock-cut shelters); a coffee or beer in a decorated coffee shop; memorabilia and a small book shop.
flags_notes: Cafe sited within the Malta at War Museum; website is the museum's - POI/identity nuance. Address: Couvre Porte

name: Ta' Rinaldu
description: A break from Valletta's museums and churches; lunch or nibbles; limited outdoor seating; interesting 17th-18th century interior; a wide range of snacks.

name: Stazzjon Restaurant
description: In an old railway station (line closed 1931); interior decorated with old railway photos; combines the old station with modern sections; good parking, away from busy Mdina/Rabat; a varied lunch and dinner menu.

name: Il Veduta Pizzeria and Restaurant
maps_search_string: Il Veduta Pizzeria and Restaurant, Rabat, Malta
description: A magnificent view over much of Malta, great by day and better at night with village lights; may catch fireworks during summer village feasts; a good menu for all tastes.

name: Danny's Malta
description: Something different for lunch or a snack; also serves gluten-free and vegetarian food prepared in a modern way; book a table or order online for takeaway.
flags_notes: Photo on page 23. Street: Imriehel Bypass

name: Sapana Indian
description: Name means 'dream'; located a few metres from the bay of Xlendi; described as the only Indian restaurant in Gozo; vegetarian options.

name: Soul Food
description: Tasty and healthy food including vegetarian and Indian-inspired dishes; on a main street of Valletta behind the Grand Master's Palace; near the city's cultural and historical venues.
